analysis.title: Everything Ends Badly, Otherwise It Wouldn't End
key_insights: As of about 3:15pm ET on Nov 5, 2026, 86% of NYSE volume is in declining stocks, which would be the first 80%+ day in nearly a year. Every sector is down, 10 of 11 by more than 1%.
VIX is up about 10 points, put/call ratios are spiking, and SPY volume is likely the heaviest since the March lows. BTIG calls these good signs for a potential bottom.

Coming into the day nearly a quarter of SPX stocks were overbought and 70% closed above their 200 DMA, a top-decile reading over the last two years. BTIG says it is hard to bottom when breadth is topping.
BTIG targeted the SPX 200 DMA at 7323 and the index reached 7362. Given the extremes, it expects some consolidation here, but ultimately a test closer to 7,000 with broader breadth deterioration.

Semis have a confirmed six-month top. BTIG targets the April breakout point for SOXX, another 10-13% lower, which would fully unwind the move it believes began in April. Risk/reward for a bounce improves closer to that level.
Rallies in semis back toward $150-$155 are likely opportunities to reduce risk.
Healthcare (XLV) and staples (XLP) look the most vulnerable on risk/reward. They are exposed to a factor unwind if semis bounce, and are still falling if semis keep dropping.

tension_points.bull_case: Capitulation signals are present: 86% of NYSE volume in decliners, VIX up about 10 points, spiking put/call ratios and heavy SPY volume.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth was topping, with 70% of SPX above the 200 DMA and nearly a quarter of stocks overbought, so a test closer to 7,000 is likely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A major bottom is hard to find when more than 60% of SPX names are above their 200 DMA, so a bottom call needs that reading to fall well below 60%.
